To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lung pericytes are transcriptionally responsive to alveoli content from both uninjury and injury, but that injured BALF elicit a more sustained response that is characterized by inflammatory, angiogenic and migratory changes.
Lung pericyte like cells are responsive to alveoli compartment content from uninjured and injured lung.
lung pericytes are transcriptionally reprogrammed and exhibit phenotypic changes in the setting of ALI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the cellular and molecular mechanisms that contribute to lung injury and repair.
the biology and pathophysiology of pericyte cells in lung injury and repair.
the biology of the lung pericyte-like cell in lung injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

pericyte-like cell transcriptional and functional changes in the setting of sterile ALI are distinct from those in uninjured lungs, and these changes are likely to be involved in the pathophysiology of ALI.

the transcriptional response of pericyte cells is more sustained after treatment with injured BALF, and the functional enrichment analysis revealed activation of inflammatory and angiogenic pathways and downregulation of tissue development and remodeling pathways.
lung pericyte-like stromal cells exhibit a robust and dynamic transcriptional response to the local milieu in the alveolar compartment in acute lung injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pericyte-like cell activation is a key component of acute lung injury and is a potential therapeutic target.

lung pericyte-like stromal cells are highly plastic cells with the ability to respond to the microenvironment in the setting of lung injury, and that they are important in the inflammatory response to injury.
pericyte-like cell activation by injured BALF leads to an inflammatory phenotype that may promote angiogenesis and cell migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lung pericytes are highly sensitive to the alveolar compartment and can be activated by alveolar contents from both healthy and diseased lungs.
pericyte-like cell responses are dynamic in the setting of ALI, and their functional adaptations may contribute to the pathophysiology and resolution of acute lung injury.
lung pericyte-like cell are activated by alveolar compartment components from both uninjured (control) and injured (rhFas-L) lungs.
